D: Helen heads out on a hero mission while Bob stays home with the kids and a baby with too many powers.
P: Serve dessert when Jack-Jack fights the raccoon for a cookie.
S: Jack-Jack and the cookie that calms him down
Chewy chocolate chip cookies baked at 180C for 10 minutes, still soft in the middle, piled on a plate.
Violet's date at the Happy Platter
Beef sliders with cheddar and pickles on soft buns, with a little bowl of fries.
Puff pastry spread with pesto and parmesan, rolled, sliced into spirals and baked at 200C for 15 minutes.

Spaghetti bolognese of beef, carrot, celery and tomato simmered an hour, with parmesan and garlic bread.

s.note: Jack-Jack and the cookie that calms him down
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g brown sugar, an egg and vanilla. Mix in 225g flour and 150g dark chocolate chips. Roll into balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes until soft in the middle. Keep them handy to stop any baby from bursting into flames.

Spread 2 sheets of puff pastry with basil pesto and sprinkle with grated parmesan. Roll up tightly and slice into rounds. Lay on a tray, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Do not stare at the spirals too long.

m.note: Bob trying to help Dash with maths
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince, then add diced carrot and celery and soften. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer for an hour. Toss with 500g spaghetti and plenty of parmesan. Math is math, but dinner is dinner.

w.note: Jack-Jack battling the raccoon in the yard
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes. Cut into squares and serve each with a glass of cold milk. Watch out for raccoons by the bins.

d.how: Simmer 150g raspberries with 100g sugar and 100ml water for 5 minutes, then strain to make a syrup. Mix with the juice of 4 lemons and 1L cold water in a jug, add ice and the rest of the raspberries, and stir well.
